h1: The 7 Best Printers for Teachers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Teachers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven printers for teachers, from Brother lasers to Epson and HP ink-tank models, compared on worksheet volume and ink cost.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best fit for heavy worksheet printing, with a monochrome laser engine, duplex and scanning. The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 wins on ink cost for color work, the Brother HL-L3220CDW suits shared color laser printing, and the Epson WF-2930 is the paperless-grading pick with an automatic feeder.
intro: Teachers print more pages than almost anyone, and the real cost of a printer is the ink or toner it eats across a school year. A cheap inkjet that costs little on day one can burn through a stipend in a few months of worksheets, which is the trap most buyers walk into.

We ranked seven printers on paper for classroom and home-grading use, focusing on print engine, duplexing, document feeders and ink or toner economics. Order comes from the spec sheet and owner reports, with no page-yield numbers invented.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser
products.verdict: A compact laser that handles daily worksheets, copies and scans.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a wireless monochrome laser with automatic duplex printing, built-in copy and scan, and mobile printing. Its compact body suits a classroom desk, and it sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks first because black-and-white worksheets are the bulk of a teacher's printing, and lasers handle that volume without the dried-ink issues of inkjets. The tradeoff versus the EcoTank is no color.

Buy it for daily handouts and quizzes. The caveat is the upfront cost, which is higher than the inkjets.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Refillable tanks keep color printing affordable on a fixed stipend.
products.description:
The ET-2400 uses a cartridge-free EcoTank system with bottled ink refills included, and it prints, scans and copies in color over WiFi. It is built for steady everyday printing and costs mid-range money.

Second place comes from refill ink costing far less than cartridges over a year, which makes it the better color value than the Canon. It is slower to get started than a laser and lacks a listed document feeder.

Choose it for color-heavy classrooms. The caveat is the tank body, which takes up more space.
products.idealFor: Color printing on a fixed budget.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: Color laser at up to 19 PPM for shared department use.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a color laser printing up to 19 pages per minute, with a 250-sheet tray, automatic duplex and wireless printing. It is print-only, priced like a department purchase.

Third place goes to a color laser whose output stays consistent for diagrams and worksheets, though it cannot scan or copy like the DCP-L2640DW. The big tray means fewer refills.

Buy it for a department or a shared classroom. The caveat is that color toner is a higher running cost.

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: Two years of ink in the box, but no document feeder.
products.description:
The Smart Tank 5101 is a refillable-tank printer that includes two years of ink. It prints, scans and copies, connects over 2.4GHz WiFi only and has a compact footprint for an ink-tank model.

It ranks fourth because the included ink removes ink cost worries for a long stretch, yet the 2.4GHz-only WiFi and missing document feeder hold it behind the Epson. It lands in the $100-200 bucket.

Buy it if budgeting for ink is the priority. The caveat is that classroom WiFi often runs on 5GHz.

products.name: Epson Workforce WF-2930 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Automatic feeder and duplex make scan-to-cloud grading practical.
products.description:
The WF-2930 is a color inkjet all-in-one that prints, scans, copies and faxes. It has an automatic document feeder, automatic two-sided printing and a 1.4 inch color display, with cartridge-based ink.

It ranks fifth because the feeder is the hero for digitizing stacks of student work, but cartridge ink costs more over time than the tank models. It sits in the $50-100 bucket.

Choose it for scanning assignments. The caveat is the running cost of cartridges.
products.skipIf: You print hundreds of pages weekly.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet
products.verdict: A fuller inkjet with fax, feeder and a one-year Instant Ink trial.
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 8139 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with print, scan, copy and fax, an automatic document feeder, automatic duplex and a one-year Instant Ink trial. It lists AI-capable printing.

It ranks sixth because its value hinges on the Instant Ink subscription, and it costs more than the WF-2930 for similar capabilities. It falls in the $100-200 bucket.

Buy it if you want the trial plan and fax. The caveat is that subscription ink may not suit every teacher.
products.idealFor: Home-office teachers needing full document handling.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small duplexing inkjet for rubrics and parent letters at home.
products.description:
The TS6520 is a color inkjet with duplex printing, a built-in copier and scanner, a 1.42 inch OLED display and a compact body. It uses cartridge-based ink and sits in the $50-100 bucket.

It ranks last because cartridge ink and no feeder make it a poor match for classroom volume. The upside is its small size for a home desk.

Buy it for light grading and notes. The caveat is the ongoing cost of cartridges.
products.idealFor: Light home grading and parent notes.

methodology.title: Print engine
methodology.description: We compared laser, cartridge inkjet and ink-tank designs for classroom volumes.

methodology.title: Running cost
methodology.description: We favored refillable tanks and lasers over cartridge-based ink for heavy use.

methodology.title: Document handling
methodology.description: Feeders and duplexing earned credit for scanning and saving paper.

methodology.title: Footprint and WiFi
methodology.description: We noted compact bodies and WiFi limits like 2.4GHz only.

methodology.title: Price bucket fit
methodology.description: We weighed each against its bucket, from $50-100 up to $200-500.

whatMatters.detail: Lasers use toner and suit black-and-white volume, while inkjets handle color and photos. Toner does not dry out, which helps over school breaks. The title names the engine, so check it first.
Tank printers use bottled ink instead of cartridges, which lowers the cost per page. They are bulkier. Look for the words EcoTank or Smart Tank and note what ink is included in the box.
Duplex prints both sides of a sheet automatically, halving paper use for worksheets. Check the spec bullets for automatic 2-sided printing rather than manual duplex.
A feeder scans stacks of pages without placing each on the glass. It speeds up grading and digitizing. Look for ADF in the listing, since the HP Smart Tank 5101 notes it has none.
Some printers connect only on 2.4GHz WiFi, which can be an issue on school networks. Check the listing for 2.4GHz or 5GHz wording before buying.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Toner holds up over breaks and handles heavy text volume. The Brother DCP-L2640DW and HL-L3220CDW are lasers.

cards.label: Ink tank
cards.text: Refillable tanks cut color cost per page. The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank 5101 use tanks.

howToChoose.note: Most teachers printing text should default to laser; color-heavy rooms should pick a tank.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Automatic duplex, wireless printing, a large tray and a low cost per page.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Brother HL-L3220CDW offers a 250-sheet tray and duplex, while the DCP-L2640DW adds copy and scan.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print daily or in color for a whole department, which points to the Brother lasers.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print occasionally. The Epson WF-2930 or Canon TS6520 cover home use.

faq.q: Is a laser or inkjet better for teachers?
faq.a: Lasers suit heavy black-and-white work and long breaks. Inkjets and tanks suit color.

faq.q: Will the HP Smart Tank connect to school WiFi?
faq.a: It lists 2.4GHz only, so check your network before relying on it.

faq.q: Is the EcoTank worth it over the Canon?
faq.a: For regular printing, yes. Bottled refills cost far less than cartridges.
Judging by upfront price. Cartridge ink can cost more in a year than a pricier tank or laser.

faq.q: How do I scan to the cloud?
faq.a: Use the manufacturer's mobile app with a scanner such as the WF-2930's feeder.

faq.q: Does the HP OfficeJet need a subscription?
faq.a: It includes a one-year Instant Ink trial. Read the terms before continuing the plan.

finalTake: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the most practical pick for worksheet-heavy teachers. Choose the Epson EcoTank ET-2400 when color matters, the Brother HL-L3220CDW for shared color printing, and the Epson WF-2930 for paperless grading.
